assistant.hello.doc: A greeting and nothing else ("hi", "good morning"): the bot says its greeting line, without the model.
not: hi, add milk to the shopping list

assistant.remindMe.everyone.doc: A reminder for everyone in the household at a time: "remind everyone at 19:45: dinner" (the words after the colon are what is said).
examples: remind everyone at 19:30 to take the bins out
not: remind me at 19:45 about the dentist

assistant.remindMe.me.doc: A reminder of one's own at a time, about anything ("remind me at 8 to call mum"): a span, a clock time, or a day and a time; the words after it are what is said.
examples: remind me at 8 to call mum
remind me in 10 minutes to check the oven
not: remind me an hour before the dentist

lists.addToList.named.doc: Put one or more things on a list the household names ("melk en kaas" are two).
examples: add milk to the shopping list
not: add a comment to the agenda later please

tasks.listMine.who.doc: Someone else's open chores, by the name the person uses for them ("what does Bob have to do").
examples: what does Bob still have to do
What does Ann have to do?
not: what do i still have to do
what does it have to do

lists.listEntries.need.doc: "What do we need?" — read the household's shopping list (with or without a shop or place after it).
examples: What do we still need at the market?

lists.listEntries.named.doc: Read what is on a list the household names (the agenda reads its appointments).
not: what do i still have to do

examples: what do i still have to do
not: what do i do with the milk

tasks.listOpen.words.doc: Who does a chore, and when: the open chores whose words hold the words said ("who does the lamp").

assistant.weekOverview.doc: The person's week: their chores, the appointments, what is open.

assistant.weekOverview.day.doc: One day of the person's week: that day's appointments with who comes, and its chores with who does them.

lists.markListItemDone.stated.doc: Something is done, bought or fixed: tick it off (a chore is completed). Mostly a reply to the bot's own reminder.

assistant.reminders.off.doc: The person switches their own reminders off.

assistant.reminders.on.doc: The person switches their own reminders on again.

lists.addToList.task.doc: A new chore on the chores list, without a who or a day.
not: new task for me: windows, tomorrow

tasks.claimTask.doc: The person takes a chore ("I'll do the windows"). Words that name no chore go to the model.

lists.removeFromList.doc: Take something off a list (a mistake, or no longer needed). Words that name nothing go to the model.
examples: take the milk off the shopping list

lists.shopVisit.doc: At a shop: the general shopping list and that shop's own list(s).
not: i am at the Lidl, been there already

lists.createList.doc: Make a new list (anyone in the household).
examples: create a new list called Holiday

lists.addToList.choreFor.doc: A new chore for a person (me, or a name), optionally with a day after a comma.
examples: new task for me: clean the windows, tomorrow
not: new task for me: windows, end of the month

calendar.addEvent.dayTime.doc: An appointment: a short title, a day and a time ("tandarts morgen om 10 uur"). A sentence about someone, or without a time, is not one.

circle.addItem.typed.doc: In a household circle: put one or more things on a typed list (shopping, chores, repairs, the agenda).
examples: add bananas to the shopping list
not: add a note to the garage

circle.addItem.untyped.doc: In a household circle: add something without naming the list — the app asks which ("voeg toe: X" always; a plain "voeg X toe" only when no conversation is under way, else the model decides).

circle.markComplete.stated.doc: In a household circle: something is bought or done — tick it off by its words.

circle.listOpen.typed.doc: In a household circle: read a typed list (shopping, chores, repairs, the agenda).

circle.listTasks.read.doc: In a household circle: read the tasks.

_family.doc: Cue words per tool family: which of the model's tools a line can concern. A family leaves the offered tools only when none of its words is in the line and another family's is; the lists always stay. Words, not phrases: a cue is found anywhere in the line.

_lead.doc: How a person opens a line that says what they will do ("IK MOET vrijdag naar de tandarts"): not part of the thing's title. Stripped from the start of an appointment's title the "+" reads, longest first.

_ownFamily.doc: The own "+"'s extra tool families (beside `_family`), keyed on the app whose ops they keep: the own note (household's note ops). Asked only by the own door (`narrowCatalogueForLine(..., {own: true})`): in a circle the household app also carries the lists, so it is never a family there.

_rare.doc: Acts a person rarely means (put a removed list or entry back, change an entry, remove a whole list): the own "+" offers these tools to its model only when the line names one of them, in `words` (whole words). `ops`: the op ids.

_refers.doc: Words that point back at something said before ("zet DAT morgen in mijn agenda"), and the words around them in such a request (`around`). A line the "+" would read as an appointment by its day alone, holding a pointing word and nothing else but `around` words, is not read by the fixed phrases: only the person's own model, which has the previous turns, knows what it points at. "onthoud dat de vuilnis dinsdag buiten gaat" still reads (it says what). Articles that also point ("het", "die") are left out of `words`.

_help.doc: Whole lines that ask the assistant for help ("help", "?"): it answers with what it can do. Read whole, case and trailing punctuation aside; a person may write either language. `questions`: how a line OPENS when it asks how something works ("hoe …"): only such a line is looked up in the help cards (their matcher alone hits ordinary lines on a keyword).

_trailing.doc: Single words that, AFTER an item, mean it is done ("afwas klaar"). Dutch speakers code-switch, so English ones may be here too.

household.add:note.remember.doc: A note for the household, in the person's own words ("remember that the bins go out on Tuesday"): what people want everyone (and the bot) to know.
examples: remember that the bins go out on Tuesday
Remember: the wifi code is on the fridge

household.list:note.ask.doc: The household's notes, read out ("what notes are there").
not: what is on the shopping list

household.remove:note.forget.doc: Take a note away by words from it ("forget the note about the wifi"); only its maker or an admin may.
examples: forget the note about the wifi

assistant.feedback.doc: Feedback about the app itself ("feedback voor Frits: …"): the bot says where app feedback goes, without the model — it never stores or forwards it.
examples: Feedback for Frits: the button does nothing
feedback: the list does not refresh
not: what do you think of the feedback

lists.listDone.history.doc: What was done in the last days ("wat is er deze week gedaan"): the household's history of ticked and completed things; today, yesterday or the week.
